item.title: Warner Bros. Discovery’s Shareholder Vote Signals the Industry’s Shift From Expansion to Extraction - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Warner Bros. Discovery has set an April 23 shareholder vote to approve its $110 billion sale to Paramount Skydance, marking the final procedural step before closing and signaling the deal has shifted fully into execution. The $31 per share offer, representing a 147% premium, secures shareholder approval while transferring timing and execution risk to the buyer, with the combined company expected to operate under a ~$79 billion debt load.

item.title: Basics of Streaming: Why Music Streaming Runs On A Completely Different Economic Model - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Basics of Streaming breaks down how music streaming operates on a licensing-driven, per-stream cost model that ties revenue directly to usage, unlike video streaming where subscription fees aren’t tied to consumption. It highlights how this structure limits margin expansion, shifts leverage to rights holders, and forces platforms to compete on scale, discovery, and user experience instead of ownership or exclusivity. item.title: The Engagement Machine Is Now a Legal Liability - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Meta and Google were found liable by a California jury for designing engagement-driven products that contributed to a young user’s depression and anxiety, with $6 million awarded in damages. The verdict reframes core product mechanics like infinite scroll, autoplay, and notifications as legal risks, with the jury determining these systems were a “substantial factor” in shaping harmful behavior. item.title: The $150bn Streaming Economy Is Built on Fewer Users Paying More - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Ampere Analysis says the streaming industry crossed $150bn in subscription revenue, but the real story isn’t growth in users. Revenue is climbing for a different reason, as pricing moves and ad-supported tiers reshape how the business actually works. What’s happening beneath the surface signals a much bigger shift in how streaming companies make money going forward.

item.title: Netflix’s Warsaw Office Turns Regional Expansion Into an Integrated Operating Model - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Netflix has opened its Warsaw office as a fully integrated hub combining content, engineering, and business operations, embedding the region directly into its global product and production ecosystem. The move reflects a strategic shift toward fewer, more centralized international hubs that can drive both creative output and platform development. item.title: ESPN’s Arbitration Play Signals Who Controls the Rules of the Streaming Bundle - The Streaming Wars
item.description: ESPN’s intervention in the WWE lawsuit shows it’s enforcing arbitration to keep streaming-related disputes private and under its control. The case also exposes distribution gaps in ESPN Unlimited, where uneven carriage deals led to inconsistent pricing and access for WWE premium events, putting its DTC model under pressure.

item.title: The NFL’s Streaming Strategy Has Entered a Regulatory Pressure Cycle - The Streaming Wars
item.description: NFL’s expansion into streaming has triggered regulatory scrutiny that could impact its antitrust protections, as FCC Chair Brendan Carr signals that reduced free-to-air access may undermine the league’s legal framework. The shift of games behind paywalls is turning distribution strategy into a policy issue, forcing the NFL to balance revenue growth from streaming with maintaining broad broadcast access.

item.title: Bent Pixels Is Rewiring the Creator Economy Around Distribution Control - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Bent Pixels has acquired Sunny State Agency for more than $23 million, giving it direct control over how creator content is distributed, reformatted, and monetized across platforms like Snapchat, TikTok, Facebook, and MSN. The deal pushes Bent Pixels beyond creator services and into a more integrated media operation, where distribution infrastructure and cross-platform revenue optimization are becoming the real source of leverage in the creator economy.

item.title: Ask Skip: Can Cable News Really Copy Podcasts? - The Streaming Wars
item.description: Skip calls out cable news for chasing podcast-style formats, but something about the shift isn’t landing. Networks are reworking how their shows look and feel as they try to keep up with changing audience behavior. The bigger issue behind why this feels off is what’s starting to come into focus.
